name: SheetFix — Excel Audit, Fix & Re-Check (Local, Private)
description:
My spreadsheet is wrong somewhere — how do I find out where? SheetFix finds out where — fixes what is safely fixable — then proves it by re-auditing the repaired file.
What you get (pick a workbook, click one button):
1. A repaired copy of your workbook (_fixed.xlsx)
2. A fix log — every change listed as old value -> new value, with the reason
3. A re-check report — the audit run again on the fixed file, with anything left over explained in plain English
What it fixes automatically (mechanical, evidence-backed):
- Numbers stored as text that silently break your totals
- Lookup keys padded with stray spaces
- Formulas that drifted from the pattern used by the rest of the row/column (a classic source of wrong totals)
- SUM ranges that stop one row short and miss a value
What it reports but never touches: broken references, hardcoded "plug" numbers inside formula blocks, duplicate keys, totals that don't reconcile for business reasons. Those need your judgment — SheetFix tells you exactly where they are and what to check.
Private by design: everything runs 100% on your computer. No upload, no cloud, no account. Built for financial models, budgets and client workbooks that can't leave your machine.
Proof, not promises: the audit engine inside is deterministic (no AI guessing) and was benchmarked on 2,700+ real-world workbooks. Every fix SheetFix makes is verified by re-running the full audit on the repaired file — if a fix doesn't hold up, it shows in the report.
Requirements: Windows 10/11 64-bit. Works on .xlsx and .xlsm files. No Python or Excel installation needed — unzip, double-click SheetFix.exe, pick your file.
FAQ:
- Does it upload my file anywhere? No. There is no server. The app works fully offline.
- Will it change my numbers without telling me? No. Every change is in the fix log, and your original file is never modified — you get a separate _fixed copy.
- What if it can't fix something? It lands in the re-check report with the cell address and a plain-English explanation of what to check.
- Mac version? Not yet — Windows first.
Honest limits: SheetFix repairs file-level, mechanical defects. It does not judge whether your model's assumptions are right, and it does not guarantee an error-free workbook — the re-check report shows exactly what remains.
